transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-10 14:00 PT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Amira Khan (Cloudline VP AI), Priya Menon (Lead ML Eng), David Rowe (SRE)

Summary: quick review of last week's model comparisons, focused tabletop exercise to agree on model pinning rules (fence) and exact escape-hatch/rollback triggers. Agreed to a short playbook and a follow-up 24h sweep.

Topics: model selection metrics, pinning policy, escalation & rollback steps, observable thresholds, test plans for canary and emergency unpinning.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Liam: ok hey everyone thanks for joining on a Thursday, I'll just kick us off — this is our weekly POC checkpoint for Cloudline. main agenda today is the fence — like, how we pin versions in prod — and the escape hatch tabletop.
[00:18] Amira: thanks Liam, yeah we want this tight because the dataset for recommendations is super sensitive and we cannot have regressions hitting customers.
[00:27] Sofia: quick reminder of where we left off — last week we ran the A/B across the two candidate models, variant-a (gpt-ish open-model) and variant-b (smaller, quantized runtimes). metrics were latency, token cost, and top-line quality from the evaluation harness.
[00:42] Priya: and recall we saw the smaller model had ~20% lower cost but some drop on the neg-handling prompts, which matter for safety.
[00:53] David: also we see tail latency spikes in hosted at certain hours — still investigating whether that's network or queueing.
[01:03] Liam: okay so fence = when you pin a route to a model and only allow controlled rollouts. escape hatch = the emergency rules to unpin/swap back. table-top is to draw exact triggers and responsibilities.
[01:18] Amira: can we capture a concrete SLA — like acceptable quality drift thresholds? we need something we can operationalize.
[01:25] Sofia: yes from our evals we propose the following as signals: a rolling 30-minute drop in eval accuracy > 4% OR a surge in safety classifier hits > 3x baseline OR sustained latency p95 increase > 200ms for 10 minutes. Any single signal should trigger a fast-path triage; two signals should auto-flag for rollback.
[01:47] Priya: hmm 4% seems... a bit arbitrary — can we tie that to top-10 prompt families? some families are more business-critical, so weighted thresholds?
[01:56] Liam: totally, playbook should say critical families have a 2% tolerance, others 6%. that's easy to encode in the gating rule.
[02:10] David: for latency, we also need to separate network-induced vs model-infer issues — otherwise we might swap models for infra noise. suggested we include a synthetic ping and queue-depth metric as part of the gating.
[02:27] Sofia: good call. we'll include host-level p95 and the runtime queue length; both must pass for the latency gate to consider model at fault.
[02:38] Amira: what about partial rollbacks? we'd prefer to route a percentage back than a full-cut sometimes.
[02:44] Liam: Redwood supports percentage-based rollbacks and canary windows. playbook will show progressive steps: 1) reduce traffic to 50% (soft rollback), 2) 10% for 15 minutes, 3) full unpin and reassign route. We should define timing and owners.
[03:01] Priya: who is owner of step 2? our infra or Redwood on-call?
[03:07] Sofia: ideal flow: Redwood SE toggles the routing, Cloudline infra approves within the console. for emergency (<5 min) Liam has the authority to cut to fallback model if the triage channel flags P0. but we need a pre-authorized cutover window.
[03:22] Liam: note that pre-authorization needs the Cloudline emergency playbook signoff. Amira — can you confirm who signs for Cloudline?
[03:28] Amira: I can sign for immediate P0 actions during our business hours; after hours it'll be David on-call.
[03:35] David: yep I'll be on-call after 6pm, I can shepherd the rollback. but if it's network we need to know so we don't flip models unnecessarily.
[03:44] Sofia: technical detail on pinning: Redwood's version gate supports exact version pins plus soft aliases. recommendation: pin to full model version for production routes, use a shadow alias for canaries so we can test and collect mismatch rates without impacting live users.
[03:59] Priya: show me the mismatch metric again — is that the delta rate between primary and shadow outputs?
[04:05] Sofia: yes, mismatch rate + semantic similarity below threshold on a sample of production prompts. we compute semantic similarity with embeddings and threshold it.
[04:14] Priya: okay, for our PII-sensitive flows we want mismatch measured on anonymized transcripts only. can Redwood run that?
[04:21] Sofia: yes, Redwood can run privacy filters and only return aggregated metrics to you; we also support customer-managed KMS so raw artifacts can remain on your side.
[04:31] Amira: good. now the tabletop: scenario one — production sees safety-classifier jump 4x for 12 minutes. what's the sequence?
[04:40] Liam: sequence we propose: alert -> Redwood SE posts to triage channel -> run quick sanity eval on recent prompts -> if safety hits persist, soft rollback 50% and start deeper diagnostics; if still bad, full unpin and switch to fallback model.
[04:55] Priya: how long between soft rollback and full unpin? we need a deterministic timer in case on-call is unreachable.
[05:02] Sofia: propose: soft rollback 15 minutes then evaluate; if no improvement, full unpin at 25 minutes. we can make that shorter for P0.
[05:12] David: add a circuit-breaker override that allows immediate full unpin if both safety and mismatch > thresholds.
[05:19] Liam: yep include an emergency clause. we'll also include a dry-run that records if a full unpin would have happened, so we can test alerting without actually switching.
[05:30] Amira: what about fallbacks — do you have a recommended fallback model for our workloads? we've been seeing better quality from variant-a but cost from variant-b.
[05:39] Sofia: recommend a mid-size variant-c we've been validating; it's slightly cheaper than a but more robust than b. fallback policy should prefer fidelity over cost for safety flows.
[05:51] Priya: ok list the concrete fallback order in the playbook: primary -> mid fallback (variant-c) -> conservative fallback (smaller quantized) -> human in loop.
[05:59] Liam: yes include human-in-loop as last resort. also include TTL on fallback so you don't stay on conservative model for days.
[06:07] David: telemetry — we need clear metrics to show we made the right decision after rollback. recommended: postmortem must include per-family accuracy, safety hits, cost delta, and traffic split during rollback.
[06:19] Sofia: Redwood's Console can produce a rollback report with those fields automatically; we'll wire up a template for Cloudline.
[06:26] Amira: timeline question — when can we have a formal playbook doc?
[06:31] Sofia: I can draft a first-pass today/tomorrow and circulate by Monday — actually, due 6/14 as we said in next steps.
[06:38] Liam: and the 24h cost/latency sweep — we need that to decide pin vs dedicated. we'll run parallel hosted and dedicated runs with same traffic profile.
[06:46] Priya: sampling for the sweep — include our peak window between 2–4pm PT and synthetic heavy loads for KV cache warm/unwarm.
[06:55] Sofia: noted. we'll run with the same prompt sets and measure token cost, p50/p95, and mismatch rates.
[07:02] David: small ask — can Redwood include kernel-level metrics when we run on Dedicated? those numbers help us convince infra to allow dedicated GPUs.
[07:10] Sofia: yes for Dedicated we can surface GPU utilization, memory pressure, and effective throughput. we'll include that.
[07:18] Amira: hypothetical: we do a rollback and we find the issue is model drift in training data — what's our longer-term remediation?
[07:27] Priya: we should have a model retrain cadence and prompt-level regression set mapped to releases; if retrain can't be done fast, we keep the fallback and schedule retrain.
[07:36] Liam: playbook will include an ownership table: who triages, who approves full unpin, who owns rerun/retrain.
[07:43] David: security question — if we flip models, are logs preserved with original model id and version for audit?
[07:50] Sofia: yes all requests are stamped with route + model version in our audit logs; with Private deployment you can keep logs on-prem.
[07:58] Amira: good. any other edge cases?
[08:01] Priya: one more — quantized models can occasionally produce silent tokenization edge cases. we should include heuristic checks for garbled outputs and a quick regex-based detect before user exposure.
[08:12] Sofia: we have a simple garble detector; will enable it for quantized fallbacks.
[08:18] Liam: ok let's do a quick read of the playbook outline: 1) signals and thresholds 2) ownership table 3) stepwise rollback 4) observability + reports 5) fallback order 6) dry-run procedures and testing cadence. does that cover it?
[08:33] Amira: yes, looks good. add a decision matrix for weighted thresholds per prompt family.
[08:40] Priya: and include a sample incident timeline for training.
[08:44] Liam: noted. any blockers from Cloudline side to proceed?
[08:48] David: only to confirm who is on the tabletop next week for the actual drill; I'll send a calendar invite.
[08:55] Amira: I'll confirm the exec stakeholder that signs emergency actions.
[08:59] Liam: great. Recap of action items and owners — Sofia will draft the playbook; Liam will send SOC2 & KMS notes; Priya will prepare prompt families; David will schedule the drill; Redwood will run the 24h sweep.
[09:15] Sofia: one more micro-note — we'll set alert dedup windows so we don't get noisy signals during a known maintenance window.
[09:21] David: yes maintenance windows will be integrated into the console so signals are suppressed appropriately.
[09:25] Amira: thanks everyone, that put me at ease.
[09:29] Liam: thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and the sheet. talk soon.

End of transcript.
